name: Proverbs
author: Largely Solomon, with sections credited to others such as Agur and Lemuel and to “the wise.”
date: Collected over time, from about the 900s to the 700s BC or later.
setting: Instruction for the young and for those who lead, drawn from experience and the fear of the Lord.
theme: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and wise living follows from it.

outline.label: Contrasts of the righteous and the wicked

christInBook: Wisdom calls aloud in the streets (1:20-33; 8:1-36), and the New Testament says that Christ is the wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:24, 30; Colossians 2:3). He is the one in whom all the treasures of wisdom are hidden.
howToRead: Proverbs are general truths, not guaranteed promises. Read them slowly, a few at a time. Notice the contrast between the wise and the foolish, the righteous and the wicked, and the repeated call to fear the LORD.
